findings.title: Date override day short-circuits the busy-time check, allowing double bookings
findings.body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, when a date override exists for the slot's day and the slot falls inside the override range, the function does `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` (line 133-135) and returns before ever evaluating `busy.every(...)`. This means that on any day that has a date override, existing bookings and external calendar busy times are completely ignored, so already-booked slots are offered again and can be double booked. The override check should only narrow availability (continue to the busy check) rather than grant it unconditionally.

findings.title: Working-hours check rejects a slot if ANY working-hours range does not contain it
findings.body: The new block uses `workingHours.find(workingHour => ... slot outside this range ... return true)` and treats a truthy result as "slot is outside of working hours" (lines 138-151). `getUserAvailability`/`getWorkingHours` returns one entry per availability row, so a user with a split schedule (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00 on the same days) has two entries for that weekday. A 10:00 slot is inside the first range but outside the second, so `find` returns the second entry and the slot is discarded. Because fixed hosts include the single user of personal event types, every user with more than one availability range per day will lose all of their slots. The condition needs to be "no range contains the slot" (`!workingHours.some(contains)`), not "some range does not contain it".

findings.title: `end` is computed from the slot start, so the slot end is never validated
findings.body: At lines 141-142 both `start` and `end` are computed as `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()`; `end` should be derived from `slotEndTime` (slot start + eventLength). As written the `end > workingHour.endTime` comparison is equivalent to the `start` comparison, so a slot that begins inside working hours but runs past the end of the working-hours window is never rejected (e.g. a 60-minute event starting at 16:45 for a 09:00-17:00 schedule).

findings.title: Multiple date-override ranges on the same day make all slots unavailable
findings.body: The `dateOverrides.find(...)` callback (lines 106-127) returns `true` when the slot is *outside* a given override range, and any truthy result makes the whole function return `false` (unavailable). Cal.com allows several time ranges for the same override date (e.g. 09:00-11:00 and 14:00-16:00); a 09:30 slot is inside the first range but outside the second, so `find` matches the second range and the slot is dropped. The logic must consider the union of all override ranges for the day (slot is unavailable only if it is outside *every* range for that date).

findings.title: Override/slot day comparison mixes server-local time with UTC
findings.body: Line 110 compares `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD")` with `slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")`. `slotStartTime` is a UTC dayjs object, but `dayjs(date.start)` is in the process-local timezone, so `.format()` renders the override date in whatever `TZ` the server runs with. On a server that is not UTC, overrides whose converted instant lies near midnight UTC will be compared against a different calendar day, so the override is silently not detected (falling through to the normal working-hours path) or matched on the wrong day. Use `dayjs.utc(date.start)` so both sides are formatted in the same zone.

findings.title: Dayjs instances compared with `===`, condition is always false
findings.body: Line 114 compares two freshly created Dayjs objects with `===` (`dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)`), which compares object references and is therefore always false. The intended case — a zero-length override marking the whole day unavailable — is never detected by this branch; use `.isSame()` (or compare `valueOf()`). As written the branch is dead code and gives a false impression of handling that case.

findings.title: Override time conversion loses the day component, producing slots on the wrong day/time
findings.body: The new override conversion (lines 216-224) computes minutes-since-midnight as `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute").hour() * 60 + ...minute()`. When the timezone shift moves the override across midnight (e.g. organizer 10:00-11:00 in Asia/Kolkata viewed by an America/Los_Angeles invitee, offset = -750 min), the converted instant lands on the previous day but only hour/minute are kept, so the override is interpreted as 21:30-22:30 of the invitee's current day — roughly 24 hours away from the real time. For eastward shifts the same truncation can also yield `startTime > endTime`, producing no slots at all. The conversion needs to account for the day rollover (e.g. compute the diff in minutes from `startOfInviteeDay`) instead of truncating to hour/minute.

findings.title: Override timezone is optional but used unguarded in `dayjs().tz()`
findings.body: `override.timeZone` is declared optional in `TimeRange` (packages/types/schedule.d.ts) and is only populated by the new code in the slots tRPC router. Line 212 calls `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)`; with `undefined` dayjs silently falls back to the default/guessed timezone, so `organizerUtcOffset` becomes the server's offset and the computed `offset` shifts override slots by an arbitrary amount for any other caller of `getSlots` that passes `dateOverrides` without `timeZone`. Either make `timeZone` required for overrides reaching this code path or fall back explicitly to `organizerTimeZone`. Also note `override.start.toString()` relies on parsing a non-ISO `Date#toString()` value; passing the Date directly would be safer.

findings.title: No test for the fixed-host (round-robin) override fix, and only an eastward timezone is covered
findings.body: The PR's primary claim is that date overrides of fixed hosts are now honoured for ROUND_ROBIN events, but the only new assertion (lines 788-804) re-queries a single-user event type with Asia/Dhaka. There is no scenario with a round-robin event type having a fixed host with a date override plus an available round-robin host, so the new `checkIfIsAvailable` override/working-hours path is untested for the case it was written for. In addition, both tested timezones are east of the organizer's (+5:30 and +6:00, a 30-minute shift), so the day-rollover case (an invitee timezone west of the organizer, e.g. America/Los_Angeles) — which is where the override conversion in packages/lib/slots.ts breaks — is not covered.
